A2.outcome: Today I can talk about my plans, wishes and arrangements.

sections.title: Vocabulary Bank
sections.html:
Future Plans — A2
plan · decide · arrange · hope · maybe · probably · because · invite · book · prepare · next month · next year

sections.title: Разминка
sections.html:
What are you planning?

Поговорим о планах на ближайшее время и на будущее.

  • What are you going to do this weekend?
  • What are you doing on Friday evening?
  • What would you like to do next month?
  • Are you planning to travel this year?
  • Why do you want to do it?

Vocabulary:
plan · weekend · next month · because · invite · book

sections.title: Тема
sections.html:
Plans, wishes and arrangements

Три способа говорить о будущем:

  • Plan: I’m going to visit my grandparents.
  • Wish / idea: I’d like to learn to drive. · I want to travel. · I’m planning to change my job.
  • Arrangement (время и место уже известны): I’m meeting Anna at six.

Чтобы объяснить, зачем: because + причина.

I’m going to study tonight because I have a test tomorrow.

sections.title: Схема
sections.html:
I’m going to + verb → plan

I’m going to cook dinner.

I’d like to / I want to / I’m planning to + verb → wish or idea

I’m planning to visit Paris.

I’m + verb-ing + time → arrangement

I’m meeting my friend at 6.

Remember:

I’m planning to go (not: planning go)
I’d like to visit (not: I’d like visit)

sections.title: Задание 1
sections.html:
Choose the correct form

  1. Tomorrow I’m going to see / seeing my teacher.
  2. I’m meeting / meet Anna at six o’clock tonight.
  3. I want / wanting to learn Spanish.
  4. We’re planning go / to go to Prague in May.
  5. I’d like to visit / visit my cousin next month.

Vocabulary:
meet · plan · visit · learn · invite

sections.title: Задание 2
sections.html:
Complete the sentences with a reason

Remember:
I’m going to + verb + because...

  1. Tomorrow, I’m going to ______ (study) because ______.
  2. This weekend, I’m going to ______ (visit) because ______.
  3. I’d like to ______ (learn) because ______.
  4. Next month, I’m planning to ______ (travel) because ______.

Then say each sentence aloud.

sections.title: Задание 3
sections.html:
Ask and answer

Ask your partner (or your teacher):

  • What are you doing this evening?
  • What are you going to do next weekend?
  • What would you like to do this year?
  • Are you planning to go anywhere in summer?

Answer with one plan and one reason.

Extra: ask a follow-up question: Why? · Who with? · Where?

sections.title: Говорим
sections.html:
My next month

Tell me about your plans for next month.

Use:

I’m going to ______ because ______.
I’d like to ______.
On Saturday, I’m ______-ing ______.

Then ask me two questions about my plans.

sections.title: Итог
sections.html:
Today I can talk about my plans, wishes and arrangements.

talk about plans and wishes
say when and why
ask about someone’s plans

One last question:

What are you going to do next weekend, and why?

B1.outcome: Today I can choose the right way to talk about the future.

sections.title: Vocabulary Bank
sections.html:
Future Plans — B1
intend · expect · promise · arrange · schedule · deadline · appointment · decide · definitely · probably · suppose · reason

sections.title: Разминка
sections.html:
Plans and decisions

  • What are you doing this weekend? Is it a fixed arrangement?
  • What are you going to do in the next year? Have you already decided?
  • Do you think you’ll live in the same city in five years?
  • Tell me about a decision you made quickly. What did you say?

Vocabulary:
decide · arrange · expect · definitely · probably

sections.title: Тема
sections.html:
going to, will or Present Continuous?

Выбираем форму по ситуации, а не по правилу:

  • going to — plan or intention (decided before): I’m going to apply for a new job.
  • Present Continuous — arrangement (time and place are fixed): I’m seeing the doctor on Friday at 5.
  • will — decision at the moment, promise, opinion: I’ll help you with that. · I think it’ll be cold.

Главное: когда решение принято и насколько всё организовано?

sections.title: Схема
sections.html:
Decided before the moment of speaking?

→ yes, but no details yet: going to
→ yes, with time and place: Present Continuous

Deciding now, promising or giving an opinion?

→ will

Examples:

I’m going to start my own business. (intention)
I’m meeting my manager at 10. (arrangement)
“There’s no milk.” “I’ll get some.” (decision now)

sections.title: Задание 1
sections.html:
Choose the best form

  1. A: Why are you taking a day off? B: I ’m going to move / will move flats on Saturday.
  2. A: The phone is ringing. B: I ’ll answer / ’m answering it.
  3. We ’re having / will have dinner with Tom at 8 tonight. We booked a table.
  4. I think she ’s going to / will like the present.
  5. I promise I ’m calling / ’ll call you tomorrow.

Vocabulary:
move · answer · book · promise · expect

sections.title: Задание 2
sections.html:
Complete the dialogue

Use going to / Present Continuous / will and explain your choice.

  1. A: What are your plans for the summer? B: I ______ (visit) my cousins in Spain. I’ve already bought the tickets.
  2. A: I can’t open this window. B: Wait, I ______ (help) you.
  3. A: Have you decided what to study? B: Yes, I ______ (study) design.
  4. A: Are you free on Thursday? B: No, I ______ (see) a client at 3.

Then add a reason: because / so / as.

sections.title: Задание 3
sections.html:
Mini situations

Say what you’d say in each situation. Choose the form and give a reason.

  • You’ve decided to change your job, but you haven’t told anyone yet.
  • You have a meeting at 4 pm. A colleague asks if you’re free.
  • Your friend is carrying many bags. You offer help.
  • You think the economy will get better next year.

Extra: say the same idea with a different form. How does the meaning change?

sections.title: Говорим
sections.html:
Plans and decisions

  • Describe one plan you’re sure about, one thing already arranged, and one prediction.
  • Tell me about a spontaneous decision you made this month.
  • What do you think you’ll be doing in five years?

Try to use all three forms:

going to → Present Continuous → will

sections.title: Итог
sections.html:
Today I can choose the right way to talk about the future.

show intentions with going to
talk about arrangements with Present Continuous
decide, promise and predict with will

Final challenge:

Say one sentence for each form about your next week.

B2.outcome: Today I can express intentions, predictions and decisions precisely.

sections.title: Vocabulary Bank
sections.html:
Future Plans — B2
aim · intend · anticipate · be bound to · be likely to · be about to · prospect · commitment · postpone · fall through · come up · on the horizon

sections.title: Разминка
sections.html:
What’s on the horizon?

  • Is there anything big on the horizon in your life?
  • What are you aiming to achieve in the next two years?
  • Has a plan ever fallen through? What happened?
  • What do you think the world will be like in 2040?

Vocabulary:
aim · prospect · postpone · fall through · on the horizon

sections.title: Тема
sections.html:
Intentions, predictions, arrangements and spontaneous decisions

  • Intention: I’m going to / I intend to / I’m aiming to finish my degree this year.
  • Arrangement: We’re launching the product on 1 March.
  • Prediction with evidence: Look at those clouds — it’s going to rain.
  • Prediction from opinion: I’m sure prices will go up. · She’ll probably accept.
  • Spontaneous decision: I’ll take the blue one.
  • Just about to happen: The train is about to leave.
  • In progress at a future time: This time next week I’ll be lying on a beach.

sections.title: Схема
sections.html:
Choose by purpose

intention → going to / intend to / aim to
arrangement → Present Continuous
evidence-based prediction → going to
opinion-based prediction → will + probably / definitely / I think
moment decision → will
very soon → be about to
action at a future moment → will be + -ing

Remember:

I think I’ll… / I probably won’t… (not: I don’t think I’ll…) → both are fine in speech, but “I probably won’t” is more natural.

sections.title: Задание 1
sections.html:
Correct the mistakes

  1. I will meet my dentist tomorrow at 9. (arrangement)
  2. Look out! The glass will fall!
  3. I’m thinking I go to the gym tonight, maybe.
  4. This time tomorrow I fly to Rome.
  5. The film will start! Hurry up!

Vocabulary:
arrangement · prediction · intend · about to

sections.title: Задание 2
sections.html:
Rephrase

Say the same idea in a different way. Which version sounds more natural?

  1. I plan to move abroad next year. → I’m aiming to…
  2. It’s sure to rain. → It’s going to…
  3. We have a meeting at 10 on Monday. → We’re…
  4. The film starts in a minute. → It’s about to…
  5. I’m sure she’ll say yes. → She’s bound to…

sections.title: Задание 3
sections.html:
Plans that change

Read the situation and respond. Use at least three different future forms.

  • Your holiday plans have fallen through. Tell a friend what you were going to do and what you’ll do instead.
  • You’re leading a project. Explain what’s arranged, what you intend to do and what you predict.
  • A colleague is worried about next week. Reassure them with predictions.

sections.title: Говорим
sections.html:
The next five years

  • What are you aiming to achieve? What’s already arranged?
  • What might go wrong, and what will you do if it does?
  • Make a prediction about your industry or city and justify it.

Try to use:

intend to → be about to → will be -ing → probably will

sections.title: Итог
sections.html:
Today I can express intentions, predictions and decisions precisely.

choose the right future form
talk about arrangements and intentions
make evidence-based and opinion-based predictions

Final challenge:

Give one intention, one arrangement and one prediction about next year.

C1.outcome: Today I can talk about the future with nuance and degrees of certainty.

sections.title: Vocabulary Bank
sections.html:
Future Plans — C1
be set to · be due to · be bound to · be poised to · stand to gain · in all likelihood · contingent on · provisional · pencilled in · scale back · roll out · foreseeable future

sections.title: Разминка
sections.html:
Certain, likely or just possible?

  • What are you virtually certain will happen in the next year?
  • What’s likely but not guaranteed?
  • What’s a long shot you’d still like to pursue?
  • Which of your plans are firm, and which are provisional?

Vocabulary:
in all likelihood · provisional · long shot · pencilled in

sections.title: Тема
sections.html:
Nuance in future reference

Будущее — это не только will и going to. Важна степень уверенности и регистр:

  • Near-certainty: She’s bound to win. · It’s sure to cause problems. · In all likelihood, we’ll miss the deadline.
  • Possibility: They may well cancel. · We could end up moving abroad.
  • Scheduled / official: The CEO is due to speak at 9. · The company is set to launch in March. · The minister is to visit Paris.
  • On the verge: The team is on the point of signing the deal. · She’s about to resign.
  • Looking back from the future: By next June I’ll have finished. · This time next year I’ll be working in Berlin.

sections.title: Схема
sections.html:
1. How certain are you?
virtually certain → bound to / sure to / certain to
probable → likely to / will probably
possible → may well / might / could

2. Is it official or scheduled?
→ due to / set to / is to + verb

3. Is it about to happen, or completed by a future time?
→ on the point of / about to · will have + V3 · will be + -ing

Remember: register matters — The firm is set to expand (news) vs We’re going to expand (casual).

sections.title: Задание 1
sections.html:
Adjust the certainty

Rewrite each sentence so that it expresses the degree of certainty in brackets.

  1. The project will be late. (almost certain)
  2. Prices will rise next year. (probable but not certain)
  3. They’ll accept our offer. (just possible)
  4. The CEO will announce the results on Monday. (scheduled, formal)
  5. We’ll have finished by the end of June. (confident)

Vocabulary:
bound to · likely to · may well · due to · set to

sections.title: Задание 2
sections.html:
Casual → formal

Rewrite the casual message as a formal announcement.

  1. We’re going to open a new office in Madrid next spring.
  2. The boss will talk to the team at nine.
  3. I think they’ll probably cut some jobs.
  4. The new model comes out in September.

Then say each sentence aloud in both registers.

sections.title: Задание 3
sections.html:
Hedging a forecast

Make a careful prediction about each topic. Use at least two ways to show certainty.

  • The job market in your field over the next five years.
  • The impact of AI on everyday life.
  • Your own career in the foreseeable future.

Extra: add a condition with contingent on / provided that / unless.

sections.title: Говорим
sections.html:
A plan with risks

  • Present a plan (a project, a move, a career step) as if to a sceptical audience.
  • Say what is firm, what is provisional, and what could go wrong.
  • Respond to a challenge: “What if it falls through?”

Try to use:

bound to → may well → due to / set to → will have + V3

sections.title: Итог
sections.html:
Today I can talk about the future with nuance and degrees of certainty.

show how certain I am
match the language to the register
talk about scheduled and completed future events

Final challenge:

Make three predictions of different certainty about the next year.
